title: Stall-to-Save: 10-day Renewal Recovery Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a tactical, time-boxed playbook for accounts that have entered a renewal stall (customer signals interest to churn or delay). The goal: prevent churn by executing a focused 10-day recovery sprint that combines technical mitigation, commercial options, and executive attention when required. Not intended for long-term strategic re-orgs — escalate to long-term account planning after initial stabilization.

Scope / When to use:
- Renewal < 60 days and observable stall in decision pipeline (no committed next-step in >2 weeks)
- Active usage decline (>30% drop in key product metric over 30 days)
- Explicit negative sentiment from key stakeholders (NPS/CSAT scores or PLG signals)
- Competitive RFx in progress and customer has not committed to Redwood

Quick risk scoring (use immediately during triage):
- Health Score: 0-100 (from dashboard) — red if <55
- Engagement delta: percent change in weekly active routes / calls (red if <-30%)
- Exec sponsorship: present/absent (0/1)
- Contract leverage: renewal value and remaining term (score 0-20)

Compute a composite severity band: Low (40-60), Medium (20-39), High (<20). High => immediate exec escalation.

10-day Stall-to-Save Runbook (timeboxed):
Day 0 (Triage, within 24h):
- Owner: primary CSM. Actions: open case in renewal tracker; invite AEs & SEs; brief wiki; quick triage call with customer (30m) to surface root cause.
- Output: Triage note, proposed 10-day plan, kill-go/no-go decision.

Day 1-2 (Rapid root-cause & containment):
- Owner: CSM + Solutions Engineer.
- Tech tasks: reproduce any regressions, restore critical workflows, identify quick config changes (prefix cache, routing policy tweaks).
- Customer comms: send summary email with commitments and timeline.

Day 3-5 (Mitigation & value re-demonstration):
- Owner: SE + CSM + Success Architect.
- Actions: run targeted demo tied to customer's biggest metric; deliver short-term pilot or focused eval; provide concrete dashboard showing improvement.
- Commercial: AE to map renewal options to customer's procurement timeline; surface potential discount/term levers.

Day 6-8 (Commercial closure play + exec involvement if needed):
- Owner: AE + CSM + Customer Exec Sponsor.
- Actions: finalize commercial offer (time-limited); if unresolved, pull in CRO/VP CS for executive-to-executive conversation.
- Decision gate: Accept offer / Request extension (30–60 days) / Decline.

Day 9-10 (Close or stabilize):
- Owner: CSM/AE/Legal (if contract docs needed).
- Actions: finalize paperwork, schedule handoff to post-renewal success team. If customer requests more time, convert to 30/60-day stabilization plan with milestones.

Escalation matrix (who to call and when):
- Severity = High immediately (Day 0) => CSM pings VP CS + CRO slack RED channel; request executive call within 48h.
- Medium => CSM escalates to Director CS; AE primes Sales Ops for limited concessions.
- Low => handled by CSM + AE via standard renewal cadence.

Communication templates (short):
- Initial triage invite (email):
  Subject: "Quick check — [Account] renewal path & 10-day plan"
  Body: Hi [Name], thanks for the time today. We saw X drop and want to run a focused 10-day recovery to get you back to baseline. Proposed plan: (bullets). Can we meet [date/time]?

- Exec escalation note (internal):
  Subject: "URGENT: [Account] renewal risk — exec engagement request"
  Body: TL;DR: [Account], ARR $X, renewal in Y days, health score Z. Key risk: [short]. Proposed ask: 30m exec-to-exec call + authorization to offer up to [xx]% concession or trial extension.

Commercial concession matrix (guidelines):
- < $50k ARR: small credits or 30-day free extension; avoid multi-year discounts.
- $50k–$250k: fixed-term extension + up to 10% one-time credit (requires Director approval).
- > $250k: escalate to CRO + Finance for special term/discount windows.
- Always pair concession with measurable acceptance criteria (SLA, usage targets).

Tactical save plays (examples to try fast):
- Rapid performance triage: bump batch sizes or reroute to a lower-latency region for critical flows.
- Short-term free burst capacity (Dedicated/Burst) for throughput spikes.
- Prompt engineering assistance: provide optimized prompt set + sample templates to immediately reduce token consumption and noise.
- Dedicated sandbox + postmortem within 5 days.

Handoff checklist (post-save or post-renewal):
- Document outcomes in renewal tracker row (final decision, concession, exec notes)
- Capture short-term wins and monitor the three success metrics for 30 days
- Schedule 30/60/90 day post-renewal QBR if renewed
- If lost, run an internal loss review within 10 business days and file learnings to Confluence

Metrics to watch during the sprint (daily digest):
- Weekly active routes / calls (relative delta)
- Token throughput for key pipelines
- Error rate / latency for critical endpoints
- Sales pipeline movement and procurement blockers
- Customer sentiment (CSAT, Slack tone)

Sample exec call agenda (20–30m):
1) 5m — One-line problem statement + impact in ARR/ops
2) 10m — What we did in last 5 days, measurable improvements
3) 10m — What we need from the exec (decision, sign-off, resource)

Scripts / language to avoid (notes):
- Avoid making long-term roadmaps promises in the recovery sprint. Use measured, verifiable commitments.
- Don’t offer discounts without attaching acceptance criteria.

Short-form templates (copy/paste):
- Customer status email (Day 3):
  Subject: "Progress update & clear next steps — [Account] 10-day recovery"
  Body: Hi [Name], quick update: we restored X, improved Y by Z% (see attached dashboard). Next steps: 1) Exec review (if needed), 2) commercial offer by Day 6.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Confirm Finance escalation path and approval SLAs for >10% concessions (Jira CS-1124 assigned).
- Add standardized dashboard template for rapid value demos (owner: Lena).
- Decide whether to make this a replaceable template in the renewal tracker sheet.

Version history:
- v0.1 2024-11-02 — initial draft (Aisha)
- v0.2 2024-12-18 — added concession matrix & triage rubric (Diego)
- v0.3 2025-01-15 — editorial pass; clarified decision gates and exec agenda (Lena)

Next actions (this doc):
- Move to final after Finance confirms approval SLAs (target: 2025-01-22).
- Pilot on 3 at-risk accounts this quarter, capture outcomes.

Attachments / quick references:
- Link: renewal-risk-tracker-2024 (sheet)
- Script snippets and demo checklist (to be added)

Notes: informal — keep this lean and prescriptive. The 10-day timebox is intentionally short to force decisive action and avoid long negotiation cycles.
